title: Correction to the card above: the way home costs the colony on a hungry bed
question: Does a colony that walks its dinner home, on a bed where food is scarce, read better or worse to you than one that eats where it stands? That is the trade, and I do not think the numbers settle it.
context_md:
**I posted the trail-lifetime card an hour ago as a straight gain. A second bed says it is a trade.** Same change, same 36 seeds, but a third as much food arriving:

| | before | after | better on |
|---|---|---|---|
| ants that got home from the food | 0.88% | **2.92%** | 20 of 36 seeds |
| what a homebound ant can read | 13.5% | 55.3% | -- |
| food eaten | 10,842 | **6,654** | 11 of 36 |
| ants born | 6.5 | **3.5** | 9 of 36 |

So the colony navigates better and comes out smaller. On the first bed, where food was plentiful, the shrinkage was inside the noise and I wrote it up as unresolved; with food scarce it is three quarters of seeds and it is not.

**Why, and it is not the navigation.** Fewer foragers reach the food only because fewer are born -- per ant born, *more* of them get there. And an ant with empty mandibles cannot be steered by the home scent at all; that circuit is switched off unless it is carrying. What drops first is what the colony eats.

**Which is the granary again.** An ant that walks its meal home has spent the walk, and nothing at the nest banks what it brings -- a delivered crumb lies on the floor like any other crumb. An ant that eats where it stands has spent nothing. Until a delivered load is worth having delivered, better homing is a better way to lose.

I am not asking you to arbitrate the numbers. **The question is whether a colony that commutes reads better to you than one that grazes**, because if it does then the granary is the next thing to build and this lands as a step toward it; if it does not, the honest move is to leave the way home fading and stop here.

(The picture is the same plane as the card above -- the way home along one route, nest at the left, food at the right, each row down a later moment -- kept so the two cards can be read together.)
